races.name: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel "Confined" Maiden Stakes (Not Run More Than Once)
Princess Margaret Japan Cup Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Alta Regina
runners_data.note: Beaten favourite last time at Windsor on Good suggests ability, but her natural desire to race prominently puts her in contention with several rivals for the same ground; Jamie Spencer's waiting tactics may offset this, though racing against instinct is a concern at Group level.

runners_data.name: Dark Issue
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's 7/56 T14 strike rate is workmanlike but the horse's course-and-distance win on Good last time is the standout credential here — a clean prominent position is genuinely attainable and Pat Dobbs should secure it.

runners_data.name: Dee's Funny Girl
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for Aidan O'Brien's son Donnacha and the stable are live in this market, but this filly naturally wants to race up with the pace and with so many rivals competing for that ground she may find herself shuffled back in a role that blunts her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Glorious Game
runners_data.note: Won her last two starts including on Soft, and Hugo Palmer's 3/32 T14 rate is modest; she is a front-runner by inclination pushed all the way to hold-up on this map because of the field's congestion, and Colin Keane will need to manage that reality carefully.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Sky
runners_data.note: Chapple-Hyam's filly has placed three times in pattern company and Christophe Soumillon is a strong booking, but the pace shape forces her into a midfield berth she would not naturally choose — her form profile suits a race where she can see daylight early.

runners_data.name: Magnesium
runners_data.note: OR of just 74 is the lowest in the field and a recent last-of-18 run over course and distance on Good warns strongly; even in a more favourable tactical shape, the class gap is significant.

runners_data.name: Miss Kodi
runners_data.note: The joint-top rated at OR 120 alongside Nuit d'Eclair and Clive Cox has excellent form — Harry Davies is an ascending jockey booking — but her sole start was on Soft ground and a step up to Good to Firm introduces a genuine unknown for the first time.

runners_data.name: Moonrise
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding sends out the 13/54 T14 operator with Oisin Murphy, always a positive, and Moonrise's placed record shows consistency; the redistribution to a hold-up slot is not natural, but Murphy's tactical intelligence means she may travel better than her role suggests.

runners_data.name: Nuit d'Eclair
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart de Foy's filly won over this exact course and distance on Good last time and David Egan has been in terrific form; a 23-day turnaround is tight for a juvenile but connections evidently have her cherry-ripe, and she is the only confirmed front-runner in the field.

runners_data.name: The Can Can Queen
runners_data.note: Four runs in her legs including a six-furlong Good-ground win gives race fitness and experience, and William Buick's booking for Charlie Johnston is never to be dismissed lightly; she will be hunting a prominent pitch she may not find in this overcrowded field.

runners_data.name: Velozee
runners_data.note: Pat Twomey's filly has two wins from four starts with a creditable fourth on her latest outing at Listed level, and her form at five furlongs on Good and Soft shows versatility; a step up to six on Good to Firm is a minor query, but she is one of the few horses here whose form map genuinely allows her to be ridden for a late run.

races.paceDynamic: Nuit d'Eclair is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to press her hard from the off, she should settle into a controlled, sustainable gallop down the Ascot straight on Good to Firm ground. Behind her, the prominent positions are heavily oversubscribed — Dark Issue and Miss Kodi are the most credibly placed to track the leader, but Harlequin Sky, Alta Regina, Dee's Funny Girl, The Can Can Queen and Magnesium all want to race forward and cannot all achieve that in an 11-runner field, meaning several will be forced to race in unfamiliar midfield slots. Moonrise and Glorious Game are similarly redistributed to hold-up roles that are not natural to them, so the genuine hold-up division is thin and populated largely by horses racing out of character. This race shape — a single uncontested front-runner setting a measured pace on fast ground with a congested, positionally compromised midfield — strongly favours horses able to track the leader in the first two or three, as a controlled early gallop will allow the pace to build into the final two furlongs without the race stretching out, rewarding tactical position over late finishing speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nuit d'Eclair Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Nuit d'Eclair breaks cleanly and establishes an uncontested lead at her own tempo, stretching clear in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: She dictates a smooth, even gallop and uses her Ascot winning form over the same course and distance to devastating effect, quickening away from a congested chasing pack that has been unable to organise behind her. Dark Issue and Miss Kodi, the two cleanest prominent horses who can actually get their position, are best placed to threaten if she weakens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Chase Home
scenarios.trigger: If Dark Issue and Miss Kodi sit a length or two off Nuit d'Eclair throughout and the front-runner ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a straight two-horse chase between the authentic prominent types, with both having form on Good to Firm and the trip already proven; Dark Issue's course-and-distance form at this level is the key qualifier. Miss Kodi's higher OR and single win on softer ground introduces a small question mark, but her class rating gives her the ceiling to overhaul a fading leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded prominent section produces scrimmaging early and Nuit d'Eclair is pressed harder than expected, burning out the leaders.
scenarios.body: With the midfield packed with horses racing out of their natural positions, any bump or check in the first two furlongs could create a gap for Velozee or Moonrise to close into, both having shown they can finish well from off the pace. Velozee's two wins from off the pace at five furlongs suggest she can generate a late surge, and Moonrise's second at Newmarket shows tactical versatility even if hold-up is not her default.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Shock Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the over-populated prominent group causes a messy, falsely run race with interference, handing an unexpected advantage to an outsider.
scenarios.body: Harlequin Sky or The Can Can Queen, forced into unnatural midfield slots but possessing winning form on Good ground at six furlongs, could benefit from a completely scrambled pace scenario where positional carnage negates class advantage. These horses carry the lowest OR ratings of those with prior winning form and would need fortune, but the structural overcrowding of the field makes a chaotic race at least possible.

watchPoints.text: Nuit d'Eclair's jumping position at the start is critical — if she is slow away and the prominent pack surges past her, the entire race shape inverts and the probability matrix shifts sharply.

Monitor the draw-to-actual-position correlation in the first two furlongs — with at least five horses genuinely wanting the same prominent slot, early crowding on the Ascot straight could compromise two or three of them simultaneously, most likely Dee's Funny Girl and Alta Regina.

Miss Kodi's Going to Firm debut is worth watching in the betting market — if she drifts late it may signal handler concern about the step up in ground speed, which would substantially alter the race's most likely winner profile.

Glorious Game and Moonrise, both redistributed to hold-up roles, are worth monitoring in-running for signs of their riders accepting the position early or aggressively pushing forward — if either commits to prominence it will compress the leading group further and increase pace pressure on Nuit d'Eclair.

Velozee's draw and early positioning will determine whether she can deliver a clean finishing run; if she is boxed on the rail behind the prominent cluster, her late effort may be physically blocked regardless of her tactical merit in Scenario C.

races.name: Longines Valiant Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Arisaig
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who has shown consistent placed form at this trip on Good ground (six runs, six places at the distance), but Charlie Johnston's runner is a natural front-runner or prominent racer who is squeezed back into a midfield slot here because Touleen and Kon Tiki are expected to dominate those early berths; his chance hinges on whether the pace quickens enough to bring him into play from an unfamiliar position.|

runners_data.name: Cheshire Dancer
runners_data.note: Holds a headgear flag (p) worth noting; a genuine hold-up operator for Hugo Palmer who has been competing at slightly longer trips recently, and his best chance depends on a strong enough gallop setting up a sustained late run — a scenario this compressed, Touleen-controlled pace makes less than likely.|

runners_data.name: Kon Tiki
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's four-year-old arrives on 38 days' rest with a solid record at this course and trip, winning twice at the mile on similar going; Ryan Moore's ability to find a prominent position practically guarantees he will slot directly onto Touleen's heels, making him ideally placed in the dominant scenario.|

runners_data.name: Pina Sonata
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's four-year-old is 49 days since last run but has won at this trip on a synthetic surface; her similar-going record on turf is thin (1 from 7), and while her prominent style suits this shape, the question mark over genuine Good to Firm turf form is the critical filter.|

runners_data.name: Sukanya
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's three-year-old has won on Good ground but those victories have come at 7f rather than 1m, and her eight runs on similar going show a mixed record with no wins beyond the shorter trip; Tom Marquand will need more fractions than Touleen is likely to provide for her hold-up style to be effective.|

runners_data.name: Esna
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's three-year-old has run her best races at 1m-plus on Good ground, with a win and a close fourth in those conditions; she wants to race prominently but with Touleen and Kon Tiki dominating the front two positions, Barzalona will be forced to sit in the pack against her natural inclination, dulling what would otherwise be a competitive profile.|

runners_data.name: Skydance
runners_data.note: W McCreery's three-year-old returns from 104 days off with a strong recent record on Good ground including a win at this trip, and Oisin Murphy is a major positive; the hold-up style demands a race run to suit, and the near-certain steady early gallop under Touleen's control is the principal concern against her.|

runners_data.name: Touleen
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows' top-rated runner (OR 112) is the race's only confirmed front-runner, and William Buick from stall six should have little difficulty assuming the lead; she already has two wins and four places at 7f-8f on Good ground so the conditions are ideal, though the style-fit flag reflects that her best form has come when challenged rather than when allowed to coast in front unchallenged.|

races.paceDynamic: Touleen is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in an eight-runner Group 3, William Buick is expected to slide across from stall six and dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground. That tempo — unhurried through the opening three furlongs of Ascot's straight mile — will compress the field and make it fiercely competitive from the home turn, strongly favouring those who can travel prominently and quicken off a steady pace rather than those needing a strong gallop to build momentum. Kon Tiki and Pina Sonata are the two horses best placed to sit on Touleen's quarters and leverage a turning kick, while Sukanya and Skydance face the toughest test as genuine hold-up types who need more fractions than this shape is likely to produce. This field contains more prominent-minded horses than can all secure their natural berth — Arisaig and Esna are true prominent racers who have been mapped to midfield because Touleen and Kon Tiki will dominate those early positions, meaning those two will find themselves racing slightly out of role; of the redistributed pair, Kon Tiki is best equipped to still grab an effective position given Ryan Moore's tactical authority.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Touleen Controls, Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Touleen dictates a measured pace unchallenged and the field settles into a compact group behind before a mid-straight injection of pace.
scenarios.body: Buick rolls Touleen into a controlled lead, the gallop is honest but never frantic, and the principals are tightly grouped entering the final two furlongs; those who have tracked the pace throughout are perfectly poised for a sustained drive. Prominent holders Kon Tiki and Pina Sonata are the chief beneficiaries, able to reel off a quickening finish without burning reserves chasing a hot early gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overrun Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Kon Tiki and Pina Sonata push forward aggressively early, refusing to concede a lead to Touleen and instead forcing a competitive early pace.
scenarios.body: A genuine contested pace develops through the first half of the race, stringing out the field and turning this into more of an end-to-end test of stamina and class rather than a tactical sprint finish. Those with a strong staying profile within this 1m distance — Sukanya and Skydance — gain meaningful ground late as the leaders tire.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow in the first half that the field fans wide in the straight and those off the pace get a clear run to produce a sustained late burst.
scenarios.body: Sukanya or Skydance, settling further back than ideal, find the steady gallop actually suits a one-run sweeping finish if the leaders go too hard in the final furlong after a dawdling early tempo. However, both are genuine hold-up types who need stronger fractions than this controlled shape typically provides, limiting the probability of this unfolding cleanly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos Reigns
scenarios.trigger: If Touleen is squeezed or loses her rhythm at the start and the field has no settled leader, creating a messy tactical scramble.
scenarios.body: Without a controlling influence the race loses its shape entirely, positions shuffle repeatedly through the middle stages and a wall-to-wall sprint develops from well over two furlongs out. In such a scenario the highest-rated horse Touleen may still prevail on raw ability, but the muddled shape opens the door to a surprise from Arisaig who, despite being redistributed from his natural prominent position, would be liberated by the positional chaos.

watchPoints.text: Touleen's uncontested lead is the race hinge — watch whether Kon Tiki (Moore) or Pina Sonata (Muscutt) apply early pressure or concede the front to Buick, because if Touleen settles completely untroubled the controlled pace shapes the entire race.

Arisaig and Esna are both genuine front-running or prominent types who will be forced wider into the field than their natural style demands — watch whether either jockey (Spencer, Barzalona) makes a move early to recover ground and how much energy that costs.

Skydance returns from 104 days off for a small Irish yard; market moves for W McCreery's runners after a long break are worth monitoring as a pointer to readiness, particularly given Oisin Murphy's booking.

Going update: all races at Ascot are being run on Good to Firm across the card — there is no material going variance between the declared going and the actual surface, so no runner faces a surprise deterioration or improvement in conditions.

Watch the draw and early positioning out of the stalls — Touleen breaks from stall six and Kon Tiki from stall three; if Kon Tiki breaks sharply Moore may attempt to cross and sit closer to the rail, which could alter Touleen's uncontested lead assumption.

races.name: Moet & Chandon International Handicap (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Golden Mind
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Fahey; last five runs all at 7f on Good or Soft, but has failed to win in 15 similar-going starts (0W0P) — consistent but not a winner in this company, and 37 days since last run is not a concern at five.|

runners_data.name: Completely Random
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for Harry Charlton, who is 3/16 over 14 days — sharp stable form; two wins on Flat turf at 6f on Good including at Sandown, stepping back to 6f would be natural but is competitive at 7f with a solid recent profile (9/15 sim-going, 1W2P).|

runners_data.name: Great Acclaim
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's five-year-old has placed five of last six at this trip on Good ground, including 2nd and 3rd in quick succession — a model of consistency at 7f on turf; sits naturally prominent and the good-to-firm conditions here will not inconvenience.|

runners_data.name: Two Tribes
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner; David Egan can dictate from stall, but recent form reads 0-0-0 in last three and, while the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects it is racing perfectly in role here, the class ceiling of an OR 102 horse whose last win was at 6f may be exposed if any horse travels easily behind.|

runners_data.name: Arctic Dawn
runners_data.note: Colin Keane, who won on this horse at 7f on Good going at Sandown, partners him again — the most compelling jockey-horse combination in the race; trainer Kubler has gone 0/6 over the 14-day window, but the horse's own record speaks — 1W2P from 4 comparable starts.|

runners_data.name: Mezcala
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's four-year-old has won over 7f and 8f on Good ground and carries a solid sim-going profile (5/8, 1W3P); though the data places Mezcala toward the rear of the mapped field, this is a horse who naturally wants to race prominently — the redistribution reflects a crowded early pace picture, and settling further back than ideal is a genuine tactical risk.|

runners_data.name: Stellar Sunrise
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners Andrew Balding's lightly-raced three-year-old who has won twice at 7f on Good turf and finished third in stronger company — three wins from eight starts, all at the trip, is a compelling profile; 50 days since last run is the only query but Murphy's ability to find a good position makes this horse well-suited to the anticipated race shape.|

runners_data.name: Back In Black
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's four-year-old has placed seven of thirteen comparable starts (2W7P) and finds 7f on Good ground very familiar; though placed in the mapped midfield due to the overcrowded prominent camp, this is intrinsically a front-running type — Daniel Muscutt will need early luck to land a position that reflects the horse's natural game.|

runners_data.name: Extremely Zain
runners_data.note: William Haggas's unbeaten three-year-old (three from three, all on Good turf) steps into a handicap for the first time off what may be a lenient opening mark; Tom Marquand rides and the horse's two wins at 7f Good at Yarmouth and Newbury suggest the trip and conditions are a match — the unknown quantity is whether a first handicap in a 17-runner field tests the inexperience.|

runners_data.name: Akkadian Thunder
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer's patient hold-up ride suits Akkadian Thunder's genuine closing style; seven visits to Good ground at 7f for David O'Meara's six-year-old show 0W1P, and the horse's best chance lies entirely in a fast pace developing ahead — which this race shape may not provide.|

runners_data.name: Saytarr
runners_data.note: An in-form horse with four wins from six recent starts, but all at 8f on Standard (all-weather); the move to 7f turf on Good ground is a significant shift, and though Barzalona is a quality pilot, Saytarr's natural speed means it wants to be up with the pace — that berth is hard to secure in a field this deep with prominent types.|

runners_data.name: Ata Rangi
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's five-year-old won at 7f Good at York, confirming the trip and ground are not the issue; Ashley Lewis (5lb claim) takes the ride, which helps offset the weight, but this is another horse whose natural forward style is squeezed by the crowded pace map — getting cover rather than a pitch will blunt its effectiveness.|

runners_data.name: Aalto
runners_data.note: William Buick rides for Ian Williams — a combination that generates interest regardless of market position; Aalto's genuine hold-up profile is authentic (hg:t, 2W4P from comparable going), and this horse is one of the few who could legitimately benefit if a contested pace develops ahead.|

runners_data.name: Sword
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams's five-year-old has placed four times at 7f on Good turf (1W4P) and goes in blinkers; with a trainer who has taken 0/18 over the 14-day window and the horse needing to race further back than its nature allows, this combination faces a structural disadvantage in a race with no hot pace to chase.|

runners_data.name: Philanthropist
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe runs a second horse alongside Back In Black — Philanthropist has won at 7f Good and placed here before, with a sound sim-going profile (7/15, 1W2P); like several stablemates, this horse's natural desire to race prominently is frustrated by the race shape, making the task harder than the form figures suggest.|

runners_data.name: Leadman
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's six-year-old has the best similar-going profile in the race (13/15 starts on Good, 1W3P) and won at 7f Good at Newbury — experience is not in doubt; but the redistribution to midfield is a genuine concern for a horse who wants to be forward, and Jack Doughty is the lightest-profile jockey in the race.|

runners_data.name: Amazing Journey
runners_data.note: Jamie Osborne's three-year-old has won three of ten starts on Good turf, all at 6f, stepping up to 7f for only the second time — the extra furlong is an untested variable; Saffie Osborne takes the ride and the horse carries top-speed credentials, but like others, the natural prominent tendency is squeezed by field size and this horse's compact form base is at a shorter trip.|

races.paceDynamic: Two Tribes is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press them hard from the gate, David Egan should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop down the straight at Ascot. The going, though officially listed as Good for this 2:55 slot, is riding closer to Good to Firm on the day — faster than published — which will keep sectionals honest and reward horses who can travel fluently into the stretch rather than grind. The field is saturated with prominent types: Back In Black, Ata Rangi, Saytarr, Sword, Philanthropist, Leadman, Amazing Journey and others are all natural front-runners or hold-up horses mapped away from their preferred positions because the race simply cannot accommodate them — the horses most likely to actually secure a prominent berth behind Two Tribes are Stellar Sunrise, Completely Random, Great Acclaim and Arctic Dawn, given their higher class and jockey profile. With one unhurried pace-setter, no genuine pressure, and a strong tailwind of prominent horses who cannot all get their spot, the race shape strongly favours horses racing in the first three to five positions with the tactical speed to react when the sprint begins — genuine prominent racers sitting second to fifth who can track a leisurely gallop and unleash late are the primary beneficiaries, while true hold-up horses face a near-impossible task from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Two Tribes sets a gentle uncontested gallop and the prominent horses sitting second to fifth swamp them in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Two Tribes idles along, setting an undemanding pace that suits horses travelling handy and relaxed; as the race quickens inside the final two furlongs, those tracking closely in Positions 2–4 have first run on the field and the track bias toward the far-rail favours those who have conserved energy from a prominent pitch.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds, Field Caught Flat
scenarios.trigger: If Two Tribes steals enough of a cushion that the compressed, position-starved midfield cannot close the gap on the fast ground.
scenarios.body: With so many prominent types squeezed into midfield, the pack becomes a tangled, hesitant mass spending vital energy jockeying for position in the straight; Two Tribes, unbothered and rolling freely, has enough engine to simply not be caught before the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Hotpot, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If several of the redistributed prominent types force their way to the front early and create a genuinely fast pace against their nature, burning out Two Tribes and the genuine front-markers.
scenarios.body: A messy, contested early gallop on fast ground turns the race into a stamina-test for seven furlongs, and any horse with a true hold-up profile who can sit patient and produce a sustained finish benefits enormously.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Wide Draw Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the race crawls and erupts into a dash in the final two furlongs, favouring horses with explosive acceleration regardless of position.
scenarios.body: A slow, bunched affair on Good to Firm ground produces a sprint finish where raw speed and a good draw are everything; horses with top-speed figures and recent winning form over shorter trips are best placed to grab the spoils in the dash.

watchPoints.text: Two Tribes (David Egan) sets an uncontested crawl — watch whether any of the prominent types (Completely Random, Arctic Dawn, Stellar Sunrise) push forward to apply pressure before halfway, which would fundamentally alter the shape.

Back In Black, Ata Rangi, Saytarr and Philanthropist will all attempt to find a prominent early position; if multiple horses force their way forward simultaneously, the race could erupt into a faster pace than the single front-runner suggests — watch the first two furlongs for a tactical scramble.

Extremely Zain (Tom Marquand) is unbeaten but makes a handicap debut in a 17-runner field — watch how the horse handles the bustle of a large field for the first time, as inexperience in traffic could compromise a horse whose form is otherwise outstanding.

Aalto (William Buick) and Akkadian Thunder (Jamie Spencer) are the only genuinely natural hold-up horses in the race — watch whether either gets a run of clear daylight in the final two furlongs, as their chances depend entirely on space appearing late that the compressed field may not provide.

The going is riding Good to Firm across the card despite the official Good description for this race — watch for any drift in the market toward horses with proven fast-ground form, as the true surface speed may be quicker than the going report implies.

races.name: King George Vi And Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Calandagan
runners_data.note: The race's sole true pace-setter, five-year-old mare returning 20 days after a win over course-comparable ground; Barzalona partners a horse with a six-win record on good ground and she is ideally suited to dictating terms at Ascot — the key question is whether her lead is soft enough to see her home in a Group 1 finish.

runners_data.name: Goliath
runners_data.note: Graffard's six-year-old shares the same trainer as Calandagan, boasting strong good-ground form and three course-distance wins — though a natural front-runner by inclination, the density of pace in this field means he may be forced to race further back than his best form suggests he'd like.

runners_data.name: Lambourn
runners_data.note: Buick takes the ride on this O'Brien four-year-old who has won over a mile in good ground conditions; genuinely wants to race prominently but, with multiple rival prominents in the field, may find himself tracking the pace a length or two further back than ideal.

runners_data.name: Masquerade Ball
runners_data.note: The Japanese raider arrives 90 days between runs but has been consistently placed on good ground across seven outings, showing reliable form at 10-12 furlongs; Lemaire is a high-class booking and this horse's style sits comfortably within the legitimate prominent group without the redistribution complications affecting others.

runners_data.name: Wurttemberg
runners_data.note: Recent form is a concern — four consecutive finishes of 9-7-6-4 and a best OR mark that is below several rivals; though a natural prominent runner, all five historical runs shown are at distances beyond today's 1m4f, and on this evidence he is the redistributed prominent least likely to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Kalpana
runners_data.note: Balding's five-year-old mare arrives in strong form with two wins from her last three, including a course win on similar ground; wears headgear and holds a genuinely prominent-to-midfield style that sits naturally within the race shape, making her one of the more straightforwardly placed runners in the field.

runners_data.name: Minnie Hauk
runners_data.note: O'Brien's four-year-old filly has won four of her last eleven and handles good ground well, though her historical pattern shows more starts at 10 furlongs than today's 1m4f; Lordan's judgment on how to deploy her in a race with congested pace will be critical.

runners_data.name: Action
runners_data.note: The youngest in the field at three, with the lowest OR (111) and a recent form string that includes several unplaced efforts — a natural prominent type who is likely to be among those finding himself unable to get his desired position, and the weight allowance may not fully compensate for the class gap at Group 1 level.

runners_data.name: Benvenuto Cellini
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with an impressive 113-11 form string over 12 furlongs on good ground, partnered by Ryan Moore; a natural forward-going sort whose redistribution to a hold-up position on the pace map is artificial — Moore's horsemanship may help him find a better spot than the map implies, and unbeaten at 12f on good ground is a genuine credential.

races.paceDynamic: Calandagan is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge her lead, she is expected to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground over Ascot's straight mile-and-a-half. The field is saturated with prominent types — Goliath, Lambourn, Wurttemberg, Action, and Benvenuto Cellini all want to race forward but cannot all occupy that ground, meaning several will be shuffled into unfamiliar midfield positions and may race without rhythm. With only Masquerade Ball, Kalpana, and Minnie Hauk as relatively genuine tracks-in-the-middle types, the race shape is likely to feature a single leader, a compressed chasing group, and very limited late pace injection from true hold-up horses. This shape strongly favours a well-rated, relaxed prominent racer who can travel smoothly just off Calandagan's shoulder and pounce before the final furlong, rather than any closer who needs a genuine end-to-end gallop to get into it. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position; of those pushed wide of their role, Goliath and Lambourn are best-placed by class and jockey quality to still push forward early, but Wurttemberg and Action are most likely to find themselves racing out of character entirely.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Calandagan Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Calandagan leads at a steady-to-moderate tempo and the race unfolds as a tactical procession until the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Calandagan sets a manageable pace that suits horses travelling prominently with cover, and the winner emerges from the chasing pack who have conserved energy throughout; the compressed pace means late-kickers without a strong tactical position are never able to bridge the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Class Asserts
scenarios.trigger: If one or more of the prominent-by-nature horses pushes forward early and lifts the gallop, turning it into a genuine end-to-end test.
scenarios.body: A faster tempo through the middle stages stretches the field and exposes those out of position, rewarding the horse with the deepest class base who can sustain their effort over the last three furlongs; Goliath and Lambourn, both from the Graffard and O'Brien yards respectively, have the raw ability to handle this shape if they secure early position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Finishers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and Kalpana or Minnie Hauk are ridden with restraint to deliver a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: A true pace-heated race creates space for horses that have been ridden conservatively to pick off weakening rivals in the final furlong; however, with so few genuine hold-up types and the redistribution of several prominent horses to artificial rear positions, the horses most likely to finish late are not naturally drawn to that role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the jam of prominent types causes early jostling, scrubbing, and positional battles that unsettle several fancied horses and produce a messy, uneven tempo.
scenarios.body: Disrupted rhythm and lost positions open the door for a horse operating at a lower OR — such as Benvenuto Cellini or Action — to find a clear run and capitalise on a confused gallop pattern; the probability is low because the class at the top of this field is significant, but the overcrowded pace map makes the scenario non-trivial.

watchPoints.text: Calandagan's lead — if she is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a genuinely modest gallop, she could prove very hard to peg back in a field with no true strong-finishing hold-up horse to run her down.

Goliath, Lambourn, and Wurttemberg are all natural prominent types who cannot all get what they want — watch the first three furlongs for positional scrimmaging that could see one or more of these horses use up energy unnecessarily before the race truly begins.

Benvenuto Cellini's redistribution to a hold-up role is artificial — Ryan Moore is capable of ignoring the pace map and pushing forward, which could compound early congestion if he does, or leave Benvenuto Cellini stranded if he accepts a rearward position that doesn't suit.

Masquerade Ball is the most interesting runner in terms of bounce risk, having run 90 days ago — Japanese trainers sometimes need a run to peak on British tracks, and Lemaire will need the horse to produce a big fresh-run performance at Group 1 level.

The going report confirms Good to Firm rather than the Good stated in the race card header — this matters most for Lambourn and Minnie Hauk, who have soft-ground runs in their recent history, and benefits Calandagan whose best form is explicitly on good ground.

races.name: Ascot Shop Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Hengest
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner, Colin Keane takes over on a horse who has won three of his last five on Good ground; the style fit note is less about his lead role than the fact he is officially tagged as a prominent type racing fractionally outside his ideal — he still controls this race from the front and his recent 10f and 12f Good form is solid.

runners_data.name: Primo Lara
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne partners a hold-up mare whose sim-going record is modest (0W1P on Good) and who has been beaten in a similar context at Ascot before; best chance if the race becomes a true staying test in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Masterinthewoods
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani partners a four-year-old with two wins and six places over 12f, including a recent second on Good at this trip; naturally prominent and should travel comfortably in the second group behind Hengest, giving him every chance to quicken if the pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Taritino
runners_data.note: Consistent performer with four wins and seven places on Good going, two of those wins at 12f; Taylor Fisher rides and Taritino's recent back-to-back wins at this trip on this surface make him one of the most course-and-distance qualified runners in the field.

runners_data.name: Patrol
runners_data.note: David Egan on a four-year-old with a hold-up style and three places from six on Good — ran only eight days ago so fitness is assured; the headgear is notable and he has placed at 12f on Good ground repeatedly, suggesting he handles this test but needs a well-run race to pounce.

runners_data.name: Tailorman
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' six-year-old returns from 315 days off — a significant lay-off that demands scrutiny — but has two wins and six places on Good going and a proven stamina profile at 14f-16f; Charles Bishop must get him competitive early if he is to factor off such a long absence.

runners_data.name: Oasis Sunrise
runners_data.note: Grace Harris' four-year-old has won twice on Good ground and is a genuine pace-seeking type; the map shows her in midfield because the prominent berths are full — she will be competing out of her natural rhythm and the style-fit discount is real, though her recent form (3-wins in last 6) cannot be ignored.

runners_data.name: Bint Al Daar
runners_data.note: Returning from 105 days off with a visor, Daniel Muscutt has a true hold-up horse whose sim-going record on Soft-biased ground (2/15) offers minimal confidence on today's Good to Firm; the redistribution from rear to midfield is an additional complication rather than an advantage.

runners_data.name: Akho Mezzna
runners_data.note: William Buick's three-year-old has placed five times on Good ground and won at 7f but is now tackling 1m4f — the step up in trip is the critical unknown; naturally prominent but has been outpaced over a mile and a furlong recently, and the stamina question must be answered before he can be fully trusted.

runners_data.name: Ohara
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners a three-year-old who has placed twice over 12f on Good and whose stable (Eve Johnson Houghton, 8/31 in 14 days) is in strong form; races as a hold-up type and needs the straight to be long enough to deliver his run — the 1m4f at Ascot suits that profile.

runners_data.name: Edwin Hubble
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides a Brian Meehan three-year-old who has placed twice at 12f on Good — consistent without winning — and whose stamina is solid; hold-up style means he needs a gap to open in the straight, but this is a big field and traffic could be an issue.

runners_data.name: Green Falcon
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer rides but this David Menuisier three-year-old has been off 115 days and his sim-going record on Good turf is thin (0W1P in two runs); naturally prominent but has not won since earlier in his career and faces a big ask returning from a layoff against this quality.

runners_data.name: Mudita
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's three-year-old is a genuine front-runner by instinct but has been pushed into the midfield map because the prominent slots are taken; Silvestre De Sousa will struggle to get the filly into her natural rhythm, and with only one win from five recent starts the style compromise genuinely hurts her chance here.

runners_data.name: Sir Griflet
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's three-year-old wears a tongue-tie and has been held up by redistribution from the rear despite being a natural hold-up horse; Isobelle Chalmers claims 7lb but the form figures (555646) do not inspire, and the sim-going record on Good is modest — needs career improvement to feature.

runners_data.name: A Daughters Love
runners_data.note: Two recent wins on Good ground at 10f give her strong going credentials, and Jack Doughty partners a lightly-weighted three-year-old who ran only 11 days ago — fitness is not a concern; she is a natural hold-up type displaced into midfield on the map, but her light weight and upward form trajectory make her a live outsider if the race plays to staying types.

races.paceDynamic: Hengest is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 15-runner field and, with no genuine challenger likely to push him hard from the gate, he should be able to dictate a controlled, even gallop over the 1m4f trip on Good to Firm ground at Ascot. Behind him, Masterinthewoods, Taritino, Akho Mezzna, Tailorman and Green Falcon are the next most natural prominent types, but this field contains more pace-seeking horses than can all slot into their preferred positions — Oasis Sunrise and Mudita are genuine prominent racers who will be squeezed into midfield against their instincts, and several of the hold-up brigade (Bint Al Daar, Sir Griflet, A Daughters Love) are similarly redistributed from their natural rear positions into the mapped midfield. The resulting race shape is one where Hengest sets a sustainable, uncontested pace, the midfield becomes congested with horses racing out of role, and the race is unlikely to truly end-to-end until the home straight. This shape strongly favours horses who can comfortably race in behind a lone leader and accelerate off a steady gallop — prominent-to-midfield runners with strong recent form on Good to Firm turf over the trip are best positioned to exploit it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hengest dictates, class prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Hengest bowls along in front uncontested and the pace is steady enough to reward those tracking closest.
scenarios.body: Hengest sets a comfortable tempo and the race develops into a two-furlong dash from home, with horses racing in second through fifth having the clearest run to the line; the Good to Firm surface rewards those with a clean turn of foot off a modest gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late closers finish strongly
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace compresses the field and true hold-up horses find a clear passage in the straight.
scenarios.body: A bunched midfield means hold-up types who settle and find daylight late can cut through tiring leaders; Ohara and Edwin Hubble, both proven over 1m4f on Good ground and racing for top stables, are equipped to finish with purpose.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace quickens, prominent types caught out
scenarios.trigger: If a secondary challenger pushes Hengest or the pace picks up sharply earlier than expected, burning off the prominent pack.
scenarios.body: Horses who have been racing out of their natural position — Oasis Sunrise and Mudita, both genuine pace-seekers mapped to midfield — may overextend trying to reclaim lost ground, while the one or two runners who switch off best survive; Patrol, with headgear and a consistent recent record of placing on Good ground, could pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider breaks cover
scenarios.trigger: If a low-weighted, unexposed runner produces a career-best on the front-end pace and the market leaders disappoint.
scenarios.body: A Daughters Love has won twice recently on Good ground and carries a light weight, giving her a tactical advantage if she travels well mid-race; Sir Griflet is similarly exposed but could outrun his odds if the redistribution creates a gap on the wide outside.

watchPoints.text: Taritino and Masterinthewoods are both proven at this trip on Good to Firm and will sit closest to Hengest — watch whether either gets first run on the other turning for home, as that position in a slowly-run race is decisive.

Oasis Sunrise and Mudita are genuine prominent types racing out of role in a congested midfield — if either overcooks it trying to reclaim their natural position, they risk burning out before the straight and interference cannot be ruled out with 15 runners.

Tailorman returns from 315 days absent — watch the market move at post time as any significant support would imply the Williams yard is confident, while a drifting price confirms the layoff is a genuine concern.

Hengest has Colin Keane but is officially flagged as racing slightly out of style role — watch whether he is allowed to stride on from the gate or whether Keane tries to hold him up, as that decision shapes the entire race.

Bint Al Daar (105 days off, visor, sim-going record near zero on Good) and Sir Griflet (consistent poor finishes) are both redistributed into midfield against their natural role — if they meet interference in a crowded straight, others could benefit from the resulting gaps.

races.name: Betfred Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Blue Rc
runners_data.note: Front-runner for James Tate ridden by Colin Keane, won at Sandown on Standard over this trip but the Good to Firm Ascot test is a slight unknown; his P tag here is genuine — he leads — but recent form shows consistency in runner-up slots and he gets a soft lead which suits his profile, though the STYLE_FIT flag reminds us he can find himself outpaced when rivals lift the tempo late.

runners_data.name: Crown Board
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa partners this lightly-raced Chapple-Hyam six-year-old whose sole win came over this course and distance; a natural hold-up horse whose sim-going record over Good ground is modest (0W), but drop back to 8f from 7f-8f pattern suits and he can pick up a place if the pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Urban Lion
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's five-year-old showed a sharp win on Soft but struggles to reproduce that form on Good, with three of his last four on similar going resulting in single-figure placing at best; maps as a prominent type but his recent course placings at 26th and 24th at this track are damning and distance/going profile gives limited confidence.

runners_data.name: Asmen Warrior
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the mount on this lightly-weighted James Owen four-year-old who won last time at Goodwood over this trip on Good and carries a visor; a natural prominent racer who cleanly holds his P position in this race shape, the course debut is the one question but his up-to-date form is strong.

runners_data.name: Grizedale
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy on the Kubler-trained four-year-old who has won back-to-back races at Listed and conditions level over 8f on Good/Standard; maps squarely as a prominent type with no redistribution flag, his sim-going record over Good is solid and Ascot's straight mile suits a horse who quickens cleanly from the front group.

runners_data.name: Spanish Voice
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's four-year-old is in excellent heart with two wins from five recent runs on Good ground, but his natural front-running tendency means he is crowded out of his preferred spot here — he will have to race in a position that does not play to his strengths, which tempers what looks like solid form on paper.

runners_data.name: Hickory
runners_data.note: Jamie Osborne's eight-year-old wears a hood and is a natural prominent racer, but like Spanish Voice he cannot hold that position in this compressed field and will be pushed wider into midfield; at OR 93 with a patchy recent record including a string of mid-table finishes over Good and Standard, the style mismatch compounds an already difficult task.

runners_data.name: Christian David
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's five-year-old ran just seven days ago — a quick turnaround — and has been consistent in placing without winning; another genuine prominent horse bumped back into the midfield by the crowded pace map, his Good-ground form is workmanlike rather than exciting and the short recovery time adds a fitness caveat.

runners_data.name: Salam Dubawi
runners_data.note: Harry Davies rides this Jim Goldie four-year-old whose last run ended in a Disqualification and who has a decent record placing over 8f on Good; a true hold-up type who maps naturally to the rear, he needs an honest gallop to bring his finishing kick into play and the steady Blue Rc-led tempo may leave him with too much to do.

runners_data.name: Spoken Truth
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's five-year-old for David Egan is a model of consistency at 10f but all five historical runs are over 10f; stepping back to a mile on Good to Firm is a meaningful test and his record over shorter trips is untested, though his strong recent form (five top-three finishes) marks him as a horse whose profile is worth monitoring if the pace truly develops.

runners_data.name: Frankies Dream
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse whose natural position is the rear, but redistribution means she effectively slots into midfield on the pace map; five consecutive place finishes on Good ground are admirable but a handicap ceiling of OR 82 and the tactical mismatch between her natural style and the likely race shape limit her winning prospects here.

races.paceDynamic: Blue Rc is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressure from a rival pacemaker of comparable intent, is expected to control matters from the outset at a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over Ascot's straight mile. The field contains a significant cluster of natural prominent types — Spanish Voice, Hickory, Christian David, Asmen Warrior, Grizedale and Urban Lion — who cannot all occupy the positions their style demands, meaning several will be crowded back into a midfield role they do not naturally favour and will race without their usual tactical comfort. With Blue Rc setting a measured, uncontested tempo rather than a searching one, the race is likely to be run at a pace that keeps the field together until the final two furlongs before the sprint begins, suiting those who can sit just off the pace in the first four or five and quicken from a handy position. This shape firmly favours genuine prominent racers who secure their natural spot close to Blue Rc — those mapping cleanly to the P slot without redistribution — over closers who face traffic on a track where a clear passage off a steady gallop is not guaranteed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Handy Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Rc sets a calm uncontested gallop and the race is decided by a sprint from 2f out, horses positioned just off the pace who quicken well on Good to Firm have a decisive advantage.
scenarios.body: Blue Rc dictates without duress and the field compresses behind him before a sharp acceleration off the final bend; runners who sat in the first four without being shuffled back cash in on their prime position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Crumbles, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Rc's gallop proves just fast enough to string the field out and the prominent pack burns energy fighting for position, genuine hold-up horses get a clear run up the stands rail.
scenarios.body: A contested mid-race for the prominent types who could not all settle creates a honest pace that brings the back markers into play in the final furlong; horses who have been running off stronger galloops over this sort of trip are best placed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Benefits Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution chaos — multiple prominent types crowding the early fractions — creates enough pressure to falsely quicken the pace, Blue Rc's rivals tire and the leader outstays them.
scenarios.body: Blue Rc, never headed and finding rivals burning matches chasing him, extends the advantage turning into the final furlong and proves difficult to reel in at a punishing tempo; a patient hold-up horse with finishing pace may nick second late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Draw Disrupts Shape
scenarios.trigger: If high-drawn runners are unable to cut across early and the field fans wide, those with clean paths and tactical versatility prosper regardless of nominal running style.
scenarios.body: Positional chaos in the first two furlongs scrambles the expected race shape, and the horse who finds daylight earliest — likely a genuine prominent type with course form — lands the prize through sheer economy of effort.

watchPoints.text: Blue Rc's ability to control the gallop without being pressured is the single biggest race-shape determinant — if anything shuffles him off his stride in the first furlong the entire pace map collapses.

Spanish Voice, Hickory and Christian David are all natural prominent types who cannot all hold that position — watch for a scrimmage over the first 2f as they try to assert, which could create a falsely fast early pace and bring closers into play.

Grizedale and Asmen Warrior are the two prominent runners whose positions on the map are clean and unredistributed — if either is squeezed out at the start or drawn wide, the advantaged shape for the handy winner disappears.

Spoken Truth's move back from 10f to 8f on Good to Firm is an unproven combination — watch market moves and early positioning as an indicator of whether connections believe the shorter trip and firmer ground is a genuine fit.

Salam Dubawi's disqualification last time out and quick turnaround for Frankies Dream (15 days) are both worth monitoring in the parade ring for any signs of residual fatigue or temperament issues before assessing their chances from the rear.

races.name: Whispering Angel Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Getreadytorumble
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who can dictate here with zero genuine pace rivals; Good to Firm form reads 7/13 at similar going so the surface is fine, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.91) reflects they are fractionally out of role at this track configuration — they lead but may not quicken clear.|

runners_data.name: King Of Light
runners_data.note: Won at 6f Good to Firm earlier in the form string and goes well prominently; Stuart Williams yard is 4/24 in 14 days which is a solid strike rate, going is fine, and sitting just behind the leader suits their profile well.|

runners_data.name: Pilgrim
runners_data.note: 63 days off is the main query — a fresh horse dropping into a fast-track sprint can be fine but needs to be sharp out of the stalls; won last time at 5f Soft and the Good to Firm step-up in going is untested over the trip, though trainer is 1/5 in the 14-day window.|

runners_data.name: Bolo Neighs
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type with headgear (p) who has placed twice at 6f Good; Saffie Osborne rides and the horse's best form comes over 6f rather than 5f, meaning getting the trip is a mild concern even if pace gaps open in time.|

runners_data.name: Kylian
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a poor recent form string (307086) and the Robert Cowell yard has had 0/5 runners in the past 14 days; recent runs at 6f on Tapeta don't inspire confidence at 5f Good to Firm today, and Jamie Spencer will need a lot of room.|

runners_data.name: All Ways Glamorous
runners_data.note: Won over 5f Good last time out and has a strong similar-going strike rate (3W6P in 8/15); tracks up prominently and Gina Mangan's claiming allowance is useful — if they settle in second or third, they are very much in the mix.|

runners_data.name: Rocking Ends
runners_data.note: Consistent 5f horse on Good ground with four wins and five places in 13/15 similar-going runs; wears a visor, is 8 days fresh which is fine, and David Egan takes over — the prominent style and excellent course-condition profile make this one of the race's better-placed horses tactically.|

runners_data.name: Indian Run
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse but placed second at 6f Good to Firm recently and won at 6f Good — the step down to 5f is a slight question, though Ryan Sexton will be looking to get a prominent position if possible; solid form, going suits.|

runners_data.name: Desert Cop
runners_data.note: Strong similar-going form (15/15) and won at 6f Good to Firm, but this is a horse whose natural style is hold-up, mapped forward here only because the field is full of hold-up types — Benoit de la Sayette will know the horse needs to be closer than usual, which adds some tactical uncertainty.|

runners_data.name: Sir Yoshi
runners_data.note: Three wins from 12 at Good or Good to Firm but the recent form string (0-0993) is discouraging; the horse has placed at 5f Good though and De Sousa is a strong jockey booking — needs improvement on recent runs to figure.|

runners_data.name: Emperor Spirit
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 5f Good to Firm and showed guts to finish second last time; wears a tongue-tie, and at age 8 needs things to set up perfectly — a genuine closer operating further forward than ideal today due to field congestion, which complicates what is already a tricky task.|

runners_data.name: Bassenthwaite
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with wins at 5f on Good and Tapeta, but hasn't shown similar-going form to full confidence (3/7); Cieren Fallon is an excellent booking and Clive Cox is 4/28 in the 14-day window — 33 days off could mean a fresh, well-prepared horse, but the redistribution means the natural late challenge is harder to land here.|

runners_data.name: Rhythm N Hooves
runners_data.note: Wears a visor, six-year-old who has placed multiple times at 5f Good to Firm but the OR of 80 puts this in the basement of the weights; natural hold-up horse operating further forward than ideal, and Robert Cowell is 0/5 in the 14-day window — background conditions are not compelling.|

runners_data.name: Underwriter
runners_data.note: Three-year-old carrying a ⚠ fades in finish flag, which is a serious concern in a 5f sprint where the key test is finishing hard; recent form (89-800) is poor and the similar-going record (7/8) obscures that finishing position trend — mapped to midfield but true hold-up style makes a forward enough position very hard to secure.|

races.paceDynamic: Getreadytorumble is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner 5f Ascot handicap on Good to Firm ground, and with no genuine rivals to pressure them from the gates, they can dictate at a controlled, sustainable clip rather than being dragged into a scorching early tempo. King Of Light, All Ways Glamorous, Rocking Ends and Pilgrim are the prominent types most likely to track closely behind, forming a tight early group that will keep the pace honest without turning it into a breakneck gallop. The field does hold more hold-up and prominent types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate — Desert Cop, Bassenthwaite, Emperor Spirit and Rhythm N Hooves are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning the rear of the field will be genuinely congested and those runners will face a harder task than usual finding clear running. With one uncontested front-runner setting a measured tempo on fast ground at Ascot's straight 5f, this shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or close to the pace — they will be in the slipstream throughout and have first use of the rail-side ground, giving them a decisive finishing advantage over runners coming from off the pace who will need significant gaps to open.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Getreadytorumble bowls along uncontested and the prominent quartet track smoothly into a one-pace finish.
scenarios.body: Getreadytorumble sets a measured tempo on the fast Ascot straight and the race becomes a test of finishing resolution over the final furlong; horses tucked in just behind — Rocking Ends, All Ways Glamorous, King Of Light — are perfectly placed to peel out and collar the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If Getreadytorumble's lead is sustainable but the final 1f sees a tight bunch finish where a prominent-to-midfield horse edges through late.
scenarios.body: The compressed nature of the field means horses like Pilgrim or Indian Run, tracking slightly wider in midfield, can benefit from gaps appearing as the leader ties up, allowing a late but not deep finish to pay off.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is even gentler than expected and Getreadytorumble, unchallenged throughout, simply outstays rivals in a dawdle-and-sprint.
scenarios.body: On fast ground at Ascot's 5f straight, a horse allowed a soft lead can conserve enough energy to sprint clear from 2f out and never be caught by a scattered chasing pack; the redistribution of hold-up horses means no one is ideally placed to reel them in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners burn each other out slightly faster than expected and a true hold-up type finds a clear passage late.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given multiple true hold-up horses — Desert Cop, Bassenthwaite, Emperor Spirit — are racing out of their natural position in a congested rear group, making clean passages harder to find; only a perfectly executed late run would suffice.

watchPoints.text: Rocking Ends and All Ways Glamorous are the two prominent horses with the strongest Good-ground strike rates — watch whether they manage to grab the positions directly behind Getreadytorumble at the break, as whoever locks onto the leader's heels from the outset holds a decisive positional advantage.

Desert Cop, Bassenthwaite and Emperor Spirit are all genuine hold-up horses forced closer to midfield by field congestion — watch the first furlong for traffic problems on their part, as any early interference will cost them the slim chance a late run offers.
Underwriter's fade-in-finish flag is a live danger to punters: if they drift across horses late, watch for interference in the closing stages in what will be a tightly bunched field.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this race despite the race card labelling it Good — watch whether horses who prefer cut underfoot (Kylian, Bolo Neighs, both with recent Tapeta or Soft form) show any reluctance to stride out in the early stages.

Getreadytorumble's sectionals from the off will be decisive — if Tom Marquand elects to take an easy lead and coast, the race effectively becomes a sprint from 2f; if others push for the front at the break, the whole dynamic shifts toward hold-up runners who currently have no clear path.
